briefing:
# Pre-Meeting Briefing: Databricks

**Meeting:** 17 November 2026
**Window covered:** c. 18 October to 17 November 2026
**Basis:** Search results only. Figures are as reported by the cited sources and have not been independently verified.

## What changed in the last 30 days

**Traction and financials**
- Ben Horowitz's essay (27 Oct) puts Databricks at a revenue run rate of more than $7B, growing 80% year over year. Its Lakehouse is above $1.5B (growing over 100%) and Lakebase above $100M. The essay gives no further breakdown, and Databricks is private, so these figures are unaudited (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-horowitz-says-databricks-hit-7b-as-agents-outquery-people). Horowitz also wrote that agents now send Databricks more queries than people do (same source).
- Databricks remains private, with no announced IPO date or public S-1 as of October 2026. It was most recently valued at $190B (https://smartasset.com/investing/databricks-ipo-date-timeline-valuation-and-investment-options).

**Launches**
- On 11 Nov, Databricks launched native Genie plugins for ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Grok Bot. Other compatible agents can still connect through the Genie One MCP server (https://www.unite.ai/databricks-launches-native-genie-plugins-for-four-ai-agents).
- On 11 Nov (Wednesday), Databricks also launched agentic AI tools. An updated Genie assistant runs in the background and makes proactive suggestions. A separate "Ontology" feature scans organisational data (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/day-anthropic-office-push-databricks-220704968.html).
- Commvault announced "Data Activate for Databricks," with early access planned for December 2026 in select Azure regions. This is a third-party plan, not a Databricks launch (https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:a912a3a702a15:0-commvault-cvlt-plans-governed-data-solution-for-databricks-ai).

**Deals and investment**
- HP is moving its customer data platform into Databricks, with a stated aim of 40% lower costs (https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/2026/10/20/hp-moves-customer-data-platform-into-databricks-eyes-40-lower-costs).
- Headlines on the same wire page reference "Databricks Plans $3B Investment in Europe and the Middle East" and "Databricks to Invest More Than $500M in the Netherlands." I did not see the full articles, so treat these as headline-level only (https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/2026/10/20/hp-moves-customer-data-platform-into-databricks-eyes-40-lower-costs).

**Hires and leadership**
- No hires or leadership changes were found in the search results.

## Caveats
- Revenue and growth figures come from a single essay and are unaudited.
- The Solutions Review weekly roundup mentions Databricks, but the excerpt contains no details (https://solutionsreview.com/business-intelligence/analytics-and-data-science-news-for-the-week-of-november-6-updates-from-databricks-ocient-smartsheet-more).
- The company profile lists acquisitions (Electric DB, Aug 2026; Panther Labs, Jun 2026; Quotient AI, Mar 2026), but all fall before the 30-day window (https://tavily.com/knowledge/company/7LlnrDq1nEGX).

## Open questions
1. Can Databricks share metrics that verify the Lakehouse and Lakebase growth figures, and the share of queries now coming from agents?
2. How will the native Genie plugins and Genie One MCP server affect governed data access for our organisation, and what is the roadmap for agent integrations?
3. What is the timing and scope of the $3B Europe and Middle East investment, and does it bring changes to regional pricing, support or data residency?
